# One parallel work unit per list item

A node names an upstream node's list attribute as its `partition_request`. The
claim producer splits the parent claim once per item, and the fan-out dispatches
one work unit per item, each carrying its own partition key.

The only claim producer needed is the one the image ships.

## The deployment

```yaml
root: /workspace
host: 127.0.0.1
grpc_port: 9200
http_port: 9210
sweep_interval_seconds: 60
```

```bash
docker run -d -p 8080:8080 \
  -e RIMSKY_CLAIM_PRODUCER_FILESYSTEM_CONFIG=/etc/rimsky/fs.yml \
  -v "$PWD/fs.yml:/etc/rimsky/fs.yml" \
  -v "$PWD/workspace:/workspace" \
  rimsky-all-in-one:<tag>
```

## The template

```yaml
name: fanout-list-demo
version: "1"
params_schema:
  type: object
  properties:
    items: {type: array}
nodes:
  - type: producer
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          items:
            type: array
            source: "{{params.items}}"

  - type: fan_parent
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    subscribes:
      - node: producer
        type: attribute/items/changed
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    claim_producers:
      - name: claim-producer-filesystem
        selector: data
        intent: rw
        alias: data
    error_types:
      "acquire/unavailable": {action: give_up}
    fan_out:
      claim: data
      partition_request: '{"list":{{nodes.producer.attribute.items}}}'
      error_policy:
        kind: best_effort
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          pk:
            type: string
            source: "{{child.partition_key}}"
```

## Drive it

```bash
rimsky instance create "$TPL" \
  --params '{"items":[{"key":"item-1"},{"key":"item-2"},{"key":"item-3"}]}' \
  --endpoint "$BASE" -o json

curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID/messages" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" -d '{}'

curl -sS "$BASE/v1/observability/events?instance_id=$IID&limit=500"
rimsky instance nodes "$IID" --endpoint "$BASE" -o json
```

## What the product does

The upstream node writes the three-item list.

The producer splits the parent claim into three sub-scopes — the
`subclaim.acquired` event reports `sub_scope_descriptor_count: 3`.

The fan-out dispatches three work units, keyed `item-1`, `item-2`, `item-3` —
the `fan_out_dispatched` event's `child_keys`.

Each work unit resolves `{{child.partition_key}}` into its own attribute bag, so
each ran against exactly its own item.

The node's run summary reports four fresh runs — the parent plus its three work
units — and no failures.

A template author gets one parallel work unit per item without writing a claim
producer.
